newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanians drown after ship collision off Italy.
newsitem.headline: Albanians drown after ship collision off Italy.

text.p: A boat full of Albanian refugees capsized and sank in the Adriatic sea after a collision with an Italian navy ship on Friday and at least four people were drowned, the Italian Defence Ministry said.
A ministry statement said the small Albanian coastal patrol boat, with about 30 people visible on deck, collided with the corvette Sibilla which was trying to prevent it from entering Italian waters.

It said four bodies had been recovered and 34 people rescued so far after the boat sank 35 miles from the southern Italian port of Brindisi. "The number of missing is for the moment unknown," it said.
Early estimates of the number of people on board ranged from 45 provided by Italian officials to a figure of more than 100 reported to have been given by refugees plucked from the heavy seas.

More than 13,000 Albanians have reached Italy in the past two weeks on a flotilla of ancient and rusty boats after rebels in the impoverished Balkan country took control of towns in the south in an armed insurrection.

Italy, concerned that many refugees are simply looking for a better life abroad rather than genuinely fleeing danger, has ordered its navy to patrol the Adriatic and has advised Albanian boats to turn back.

The sinking was the first incident involving fatalities since the exodus of Albanians began on March 13. Colonel Giuseppe Serrano, commander of customs police in Brindisi, told Reuters that he believed two of the dead were children.

The ministry statement said the boat was first detected at around 1615 GMT off the southern Albanian port of Vlore and was approached by the navy ship Zeffiro which was under orders to prevent Albanians from illegally entering Italy.
"The ship ignored all calls from Zeffiro for it to halt, carrying out various evasive manoeuvres and continuing to head for Italy," it said.

"Later, the control of the Albanian ship was passed to the ship Sibilla, which at 1900 approached at slow speed. During this manouevre, the patrol boat carried out an abrupt shift to the right, cutting across the Sibilla's path.
"The Italian ship immediately stopped its engines and went into reverse but could not avoid the collision which caused the capsizing of the Albanian vessel."
The ministry said a rescue operation was immediately mounted, with personnel from both Italian ships, planes and helicopters later joined by coastguard vessels.

Serrano said helicopters with spotlights were looking for more survivors and the ministry said: "The searches continue with all means available, while those rescued have been transported to coastguard motor boats to be transferred to Brindisi."

Coastguards said earlier that the flow of Albanian refugees seemed to have dried up due to a combination of bad weather and the naval patrols. They said radar had detected only a single boat approaching Brindisi.

Italy has said it will grant temporary sanctuary to genuine refugees but will repatriate "undesirables". About 1,000 Albanians have been sent back, either for breaking the law since arriving in Italy or as suspected escaped convicts.
